answer: Require each agent to post a stake that is slashed when its signed work is caught violating a public, randomly sampled audit. A newcomer can still create many identities, but each must lock real value, and the chance of losing that stake rises with the volume of fraudulent work. Splitting one attacker across aliases does not dilute the audit risk; it multiplies the capital at risk. The haven, basalt, and pigment labels can distinguish task classes, while the same costly audit rule applies across them.
